title: Short-Sale Statement Balance Calculation of the Payoff and Loan Satisfaction Product
content:
# Short-sale statement balance — how the figure is computed

Payoff and Loan Satisfaction. On the payoff case of an Approved Short Sale Payoff requested by the borrower of record, the statement's good-through date is the plan's good-through period of calendar days after the statement date.

The short-sale statement balance is the loan's principal balance plus the short-sale accrual charge plus six short-sale statement charges (the short-sale statement set-aside disbursement, the short-sale statement servicing fee, the short-sale statement preservation charge, the short-sale statement called-due appraisal charge, the short-sale statement replacement appraisal charge and the short-sale statement foreclosure charge), rounded half up to the cent and only at that last step.

- **Short-sale accrual charge:** the per diem the payoff case carries times the short-sale accrual days, which are the calendar days from the effective date of the latest posted interest accrual on the loan to the statement date (0 for a loan with no posted interest accrual) plus the plan's good-through period of calendar days.
- **Statement charges:** the short-sale statement called-due appraisal charge is USD 475.00 and the other five short-sale statement charges are each 0.00.

### Hypothetical worked figure

| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| Principal balance | USD 240000.00 |
| Per diem on the case | USD 45.10 |
| Days since the latest posted interest accrual | 8 |
| Good-through period from the plan schedule | 30 |

Accrual days 8 and 30, so 38; accrual charge USD 1713.80; statement charges USD 475.00; short-sale statement balance USD 242188.80. The inputs are invented for the illustration.
